As of 2024, there are no established agricultural yields on Mars, as significant research and experimentation are still ongoing to determine the feasibility of growing crops in Martian soil. Here are some key points regarding the current state of agricultural research on Mars:

### Current Research and Experiments
1. **Soil Composition Challenges**: Martian soil, or regolith, contains toxic perchlorates, which pose a significant challenge for growing plants. Researchers are exploring methods to either remove these toxic salts or modify the soil to make it suitable for agriculture [MIT Technology Review](https://www.technologyreview.com/2024/10/17/1105135/mars-farming-soil-food-humans-farming-agriculture/).

2. **Microbial Solutions**: There is ongoing research funded by NASA and the National Science Foundation to use microbial life to detoxify Martian regolith and potentially convert it into arable soil. This approach could not only aid in Martian agriculture but also have applications for improving soil in arid regions on Earth [MIT Technology Review](https://www.technologyreview.com/2024/10/17/1105135/mars-farming-soil-food-humans-farming-agriculture/).

3. **Experimental Results**: Initial experiments have shown that growing plants in Martian-like conditions is possible, but results vary significantly based on the methods used and the specific crops tested. For instance, some studies have indicated that crops grown in simulated Martian soil have lower germination rates and biomass compared to those grown in Earth soil [Technology Review](https://www.technologyreview.com/2024/10/17/1105135/mars-farming-soil-food-humans-farming-agriculture/).

### Future Prospects
- **Hydroponics vs. Soil Farming**: While hydroponics can support small crews, scaling up to feed larger populations on Mars will require developing viable soil farming techniques. This is crucial for establishing a sustainable human presence on the planet [MIT Technology Review](https://www.technologyreview.com/2024/10/17/1105135/mars-farming-soil-food-humans-farming-agriculture/).

- **Long-Term Goals**: The ultimate goal is to create a self-sustaining agricultural system on Mars that can support human life independently from Earth. This involves overcoming significant environmental challenges and developing new agricultural technologies [MIT Technology Review](https://www.technologyreview.com/2024/10/17/1105135/mars-farming-soil-food-humans-farming-agriculture/).

In summary, while there are promising avenues of research, actual agricultural yields on Mars in 2024 remain theoretical and experimental, with ongoing studies aimed at overcoming the unique challenges posed by the Martian environment.
